title.narrative: Number of youth trained in soft skills/life skills through USG assisted programs.

description.narrative: Soft skills/life skills: a broad set of skills, competencies, behaviors, attitudes, and personal qualities that enable people to effectively navigate their environment, work well with others, perform well, and achieve their goals. This includes management, leadership, social, and/or civic engagement skills. Social or leadership skills: Training that focuses on skills that will enhance youth’s ability to interact within their community. This training includes a focus on management, leadership, life and/or soft skills, and/or civic engagement. For the purpose of this indicator, training is defined as an intervention/session (virtual and/or in person) that has learning objectives and focuses on enhancing a certain skill. A focus group, mentoring or coaching activity, apprenticeship, or internship can be considered under training if within the listed skills topics. Individuals will be considered trained if they complete 80% of the training. Individuals completing less than 80% will not be counted.

title.narrative: Proposal for a legal or institutional framework to support social insertion prepared by the Project

description.narrative: The Project will prepare a diagnosis of the existing legal and institutional framework and, depending on the current situation, will prepare a proposal for a legal or institutional framework to support social integration processes. 100% legal or institutional framework completed 20% diagnostic process completed 30% First draft of the proposal presented for discussion with key actors 50% final version of the complete document. Numerator: specific percentage assigned to each output (stage). Denominator: 1. (Equivalent to 100%, which represents the total of the indicator reached).

title.narrative: Model for the social insertion of gang-affiliated persons with voluntary gang desistance designed, validated and implemented and evaluated.

description.narrative:
The Social Insertion Model is the process that the Project will implement to achieve the development of skills and competencies that allow the social, educational and economic insertion of people who have given up their life in gangs (gang desistance); It will be implemented in coordination with the Dirección de Reconstrucción de Tejido Social and faith-based organizations. The model will also undergo a pre and post quantitative evaluation combined with a qualitative evaluation.
An insertion model that is designed, validated, implemented and evaluated, represents 100%.
15% insertion model designed - document produced. 15% performance evaluation designed – document produced. 10% Insertion model validated by the DRTS and advisory committee, ready for implementation. 30% Insertion model implemented 30% Insertion model evaluated.

title.narrative: Model for the social insertion of adolescents in conflict with the law (incarcerated) and with gang affiliation designed, validated and implemented and evaluated.

description.narrative:
The Social Insertion Model is the process that the project will implement to achieve the development of skills and competencies that allow the social, educational, and economic insertion of young and adolescents with gang affiliation serving a judicial sentence in CIS of Tonacatepeque. The model will also undergo a pre and post quantitative evaluation combined with a qualitative evaluation.
An insertion model that is designed, validated, implemented and evaluated, represents 100%. 15% insertion model designed - document produced. 15% Performance evaluation designed - document produced. 10% Insertion model validated by the ISNA and advisory committee, ready for implementation. 30% Insertion model implemented at CIS of Tonacatepeque 30% Insertion model evaluated.

title.narrative: Percentage of beneficiaries who express intention to migrate in the next three years.

description.narrative: The indicator is in reference to the high percentage of insertion-model participants whose intention to emigrate outside of El Salvador (mainly to the United States) declines. Forced and illegal migration tends to be a recurring phenomenon in vulnerable populations, given the difficulty in generating necessary and sufficient livelihood. Numerator: Number of participants that express intention to migrate in the next three years. Indicator: Total number of program beneficiaries. 115

title.narrative: The number of partnerships established with public institutions, private sector, civil society organizations, in support of the insertion program

description.narrative: The indicator measures the number of partnerships and/or agreements formally established with public institutions, private sector and civil society organizations (NGOs, academia, faith-based organizations) that will strengthen the implementation of the reinsertion model.

title.narrative: Number of individuals with new employment following completion of USG-assisted workforce development programs

description.narrative:
The number of individuals in new employment completion of USG-assisted workforce development programs. The employment compromise all persons of working age (15-29 years old) who during at least three months were in one or more (during the project´s implementation) of the following categories: 1. Paid employment, this includes: a. Persons at work who during at least three months performed at least one hour of work for wage salary in cash or in-kind. b. Apprentices or interns who received pay in cash or in-kind.
2. Self-employment, this includes: a. Persons with “an entrepreneurial activity but not at work” which may be a business, a farm or a service undertaking, who were temporarily not at work during one month for any specific reason. b. Employers, people who work their own account who received pay in cash or in-kind.

title.narrative: Percent of individuals who transition to further education, or training following participation in USG-assisted programs

description.narrative: This indicator intends to capture transitions that meaningfully advance the education or career goals of individuals. 'Further education or training' refers to education in which the eventual earning of a degree or diploma--such as primary, secondary, or post-secondary education or equivalent--is possible; and to certification-granting technical/vocational education or training. Individuals can be counted as ‘transitioning’ to further education or training if they enroll in education or training programs within six months of the end of the US-assisted programming in which they participated. Individuals who are already enrolled in the formal education system would not count towards this indicator, even if they are participating in a supplemental program. 'Percent of Individuals' is the number of individuals who have transitioned to further education or training divided by the total number of individuals who participate in programming. Individuals who are studying after participating in programs delivered by other trainees as part of a deliberate service delivery strategy (e.g. cascade training) are counted. Calculation of percentage: Numerator*=Number of individuals transitioning to further education or training Denominator*=Number of individuals who participate in programming *Activities that rely on a sample of learners rather than a census to report results should sample to ensure representation of characteristics that are important for understanding differences in outcomes (e.g., geography, language, sex, etc.). Numerators and denominators, extrapolated onto the activity population, must be reported.
